title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks
title_zh: DAEDALUS：通过自生成任务引导智能体记忆的建立

paragraphs.en: LLM agents often lack the operational knowledge to act reliably in new environments, as they must discover specific tool behaviors or environment conventions on their own. Without memory of past attempts, they repeat the same mistakes across tasks, leading to more task failures and longer trajectories. To address this, agentic systems typically rely on human-written guidelines or on procedural memory built from training tasks and an oracle verifier, both of which require prior knowledge of the environment. We present Daedalus , a method for bootstrapping reusable agent memory from self-generated practice without existing tasks or oracle verifiers. Daedalus pairs two agents: an explorer that interacts with the environment to generate challenging yet solvable tasks, and a solver that attempts them. A heuristic is derived from each solver failure and accepted only after the solver repeatedly succeeds with that heuristic in context. These outcomes also provide feedback for the explorer to refine the difficulty of future tasks. The accepted heuristics are then consolidated into a memory bank for test-time use. Across AppWorld, τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench, and AutomationBench, Daedalus improves mean success rates by up to 15.9 percentage points and pass^5 by up to 2.2 × \times over a no-memory baseline, and is competitive with methods using training tasks, at a lower inference cost than most. We show that performance gains already emerge with a small exploration budget, and that its heuristics also benefit agents from other model families. Our ablations further reveal that solver traces provide the key information needed to derive effective heuristics, while factorizing early discoveries makes exploration more cost-efficient. Beyond memory construction, we find that the tasks generated by Daedalus can serve as a proxy for benchmark tasks when ranking models by performance. We release the code and artifacts, including generation and inference traces, at www.github.com/illuin-tech/daedalus .

paragraphs.en: LLM agents are now deployed to perform real-world tasks in a wide range of occupations and industries ( Sajadieh et al., 2026 ; Massenkoff et al., 2026 ; Johnston et al., 2026 ) . As they gain autonomy ( McCain et al., 2026 ) , they operate in increasingly complex environments with limited human guidance. Acting reliably in such environments requires practical knowledge that carries over across tasks, a need reflected in the rapid adoption of agent skills ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . Without procedural memory to retain this knowledge, an agent rediscovers its environment from task to task, leading to avoidable errors and longer, costlier executions ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: LLM 智能体现已部署，用于在广泛职业和行业中执行现实世界的任务（Sajadieh 等人，2026；Massenkoff 等人，2026；Johnston 等人，2026）。 随着它们获得自主性（McCain 等人，2026），它们在没有人类有限指导的情况下，在日益复杂的环境中运行。 在这种环境中可靠地行动需要能够跨任务迁移的实际知识，这一需求反映了对智能体技能的快速采用上（Zhang 等人，2025a）。 如果没有程序性记忆来保留这些知识，智能体每次执行任务时都会重新探索其环境，从而导致可避免的错误以及耗时更长、成本更高的执行过程（Ouyang 等人，2026）。

paragraphs.en: Procedural memory is typically built from past experience: an agent attempts tasks, and lessons drawn from its successes and failures are stored and injected in context at test time ( Zhao et al., 2024 ; Allard et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) , which leaves model weights untouched and applies to both open and closed models. This demands a curated set of training tasks drawn from the target task distribution, often paired with a verifier that scores each attempt. Building this supervision requires prior knowledge of the environment and substantial human effort, as the construction of agentic benchmarks illustrates ( Trivedi et al., 2024 ; Barres et al., 2026 ) . It is therefore unavailable for most environments, a limitation that is increasingly prevalent as more and more agentic environments are automatically generated without human supervision ( Tu et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) . Instead, experience can be gathered from task queries as they arrive at test time ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , but the agent then handles its first tasks without memory and improves only after failing on them. In both cases, memory is built only from exposure to the tasks it is meant to support.
paragraphs.zh: 程序性记忆通常由过往经验构建：智能体尝试执行任务，并从其成功与失败中吸取的教训会被存储并在测试时注入上下文（Zhao et al., 2024；Allard et al., 2026；Zhang et al., 2026），这种方式不会改变模型权重，且适用于开放和封闭模型。 这需要一组经过精心挑选的训练任务，这些任务需来自目标任务的分布，通常还需要配合一个用于为每次尝试评分的验证器。 构建这种监督机制需要预先了解环境并投入大量人力，正如智能体基准测试的构建过程所显示的那样（Trivedi et al., 2024；Barres et al., 2026）。 因此，这种方法在大多数环境中都无法使用；随着越来越多智能体环境在没有人类监督的情况下被自动生成，这一局限性正变得愈发普遍（Tu et al., 2026；Wang et al., 2026）。 取而代之的是，经验可以在测试时随着任务查询的到来而收集（Wang et al., 2025；Ouyang et al., 2026），但此时智能体在首次执行任务时仍没有记忆，只有在失败之后才能逐步改进。 在这两种情况下，记忆都仅通过接触其需要支持的任务本身来构建。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduce Daedalus , a training-free method that builds environment-specific memory from self-generated tasks without curated tasks or an oracle verifier. Daedalus involves auxiliary agents that explore the environment to create solvable tasks and their success criteria, and a solver agent that attempts these tasks. The solver learns from its failures, as each one is turned into an in-context heuristic that guides its subsequent attempts. The relevance of a heuristic is validated only when it enables the solver to repeatedly succeed on a task it initially failed. Tasks that offer no such learning signal are refined to adjust their difficulty, and these refinements are condensed into task design guidelines for later sessions. Together, these components automate exploration and task creation in an agentic environment, calibrate task difficulty to the solver’s capabilities, and produce memory items that are empirically tested.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们提出了 Daedalus——一种无需训练的方法，它通过自我生成的任务构建特定环境的记忆，而无需依赖人工筛选的任务或“神谕”验证器。 Daedalus 包含辅助智能体，它们会探索环境以创建可解决的任务及其成功标准，还有一个求解智能体负责尝试完成这些任务。 求解智能体会从失败中学习，因为每次失败都会转化为一种情境启发式方法，指导其后续尝试。 某种启发式方法的相关性只有在它能让求解智能体在最初失败的任务上持续成功时才会得到验证。 那些无法提供此类学习信号的任务会被调整难度，而这些调整最终会凝练成任务设计指南，供后续阶段使用。 这些组件共同作用，能够在智能体环境中自动实现探索与任务创建，根据求解智能体的能力校准任务难度，并生成经过实证检验的记忆条目。

paragraphs.en: On AppWorld ( Trivedi et al., 2024 ) , τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench ( Barres et al., 2026 ) , and AutomationBench ( Shepard and Salimans, 2026 ) , Daedalus improves success rates by up to 15.9 points over a no-memory baseline and raises pass^5 by 1.7 to 2.2 × 2.2\times , at little to no extra inference cost. It outperforms PREPING ( Choi et al., 2026 ) , which also builds memory from self-generated tasks, and is competitive with existing methods that use the benchmark training tasks. These gains hold across model families, including when the memory is generated with one family and used by another, and can be achieved with only a small generation budget. Experiments show that validating lessons through the solver’s attempts drives these results, whereas memory drawn from exploration alone hurts the agent. We also find that, at this scale, consolidating the bank and injecting it whole at the start of each task outperforms per-turn retrieval. Beyond memory, the generated tasks rank models consistently with the official benchmark test sets, which suggests they can serve as an evaluation proxy when no curated tasks exist. Daedalus thus bootstraps agent memory in new environments without human supervision, so that agents no longer discover them through trial and error at test time. We release our code and experimental artifacts, including configurations, generated tasks, heuristic banks, and all agent trajectories, so that our experiments can be reproduced and verified.
paragraphs.zh: 在 AppWorld (Trivedi et al., 2024)、τ²-bench (Barres et al., 2026) 和 AutomationBench (Shepard and Salimans, 2026) 上，Daedalus 相比无记忆基线模型将成功率提升了最多 15.9 个百分点，并将 pass^5 从 1.7 提升至 2.2 × 2.2\times，且几乎没有额外的推理成本。 它的表现优于 PREPING (Choi et al., 2026)——后者同样通过自我生成的任务构建记忆——并且与使用基准测试训练任务的现有方法具有竞争力。 这些增益在不同模型家族中均成立，包括当记忆由一个模型家族生成而由另一个模型家族使用的情况，且只需极小的生成预算即可实现。 实验表明，通过求解器的尝试来验证经验是取得这些结果的关键，而仅从探索中获取的记忆则会损害智能体的表现。 我们还发现，在这一规模下，将记忆库整合并在每个任务开始时一次性注入，其效果优于每轮单独检索的方式。 除了记忆之外，生成的任务在模型排名上与官方基准测试集保持一致，这表明在没有现成精选任务时，它们可以用作评估代理。 因此，Daedalus 能够在无需人类监督的情况下，在新环境中启动智能体的记忆机制，使智能体在测试阶段不再需要通过试错来发现这些记忆。 我们公开了代码和实验成果，包括配置、生成的任务、启发式规则库以及所有智能体轨迹，以便我们的实验能够被复现和验证。

sents.en: We also find that, at this scale, consolidating the bank and injecting it whole at the start of each task outperforms per-turn retrieval.

sents.en: Daedalus thus bootstraps agent memory in new environments without human supervision, so that agents no longer discover them through trial and error at test time.
sents.zh: 因此，Daedalus 能够在无需人类监督的情况下，在新环境中启动智能体的记忆机制，使智能体在测试阶段不再需要通过试错来发现这些记忆。

sents.en: We release our code and experimental artifacts, including configurations, generated tasks, heuristic banks, and all agent trajectories, so that our experiments can be reproduced and verified.
sents.zh: 我们公开了代码和实验成果，包括配置、生成的任务、启发式规则库以及所有智能体轨迹，以便我们的实验能够被复现和验证。

paragraphs.en: LLM-agent memory methods allow agents to accumulate reusable knowledge from past task attempts. Many store it as natural-language insights: ExpeL ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) contrasts successful and failed trajectories, AutoGuide ( Fu et al., 2024 ) makes such guidelines context-aware, and other systems generate reflections from failed attempts ( Allard et al., 2026 ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ) . These methods retain an insight based on the outcome of the trajectory it came from, without confirming that it helps the agent overcome the failure; Daedalus instead keeps an insight only once it has turned a failure into repeated success. Others build skill libraries, from Voyager’s executable code skills ( Wang et al., 2024 ) to natural-language skills refined through reward-based optimization ( Mi et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) , which requires oracle verifiers or weight updates. Memory can also be organized as reusable workflows ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , evolving playbooks ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , or long-term memory stores ( Fang et al., 2026 ; Chhikara et al., 2025 ) . Most of these methods, however, collect experience from a predefined task set, which a new environment does not provide, whereas Daedalus generates its own.

paragraphs.en: Automatic exploration is widely used to synthesize agent training data in software, computer-use, and general-application environments ( Shi et al., 2026 ; Ramrakhya et al., 2026 ; Dong et al., 2026 ) , sometimes with curricula that adapt task difficulty to the agent’s progress ( Sun et al., 2026 ; Xue et al., 2026 ) . Self-play extends this by training the model as both proposer and solver ( Liu et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2026 ) , rewarding tasks that are challenging yet verifiable ( Yue et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) . In all these works, generated tasks serve to update model weights. Few methods generate tasks to build memory instead: Voyager ( Wang et al., 2024 ) proposes tasks through an automatic curriculum, SkillWeaver ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) practices self-proposed skills on websites, and PREPING ( Choi et al., 2026 ) , closest to our setting, builds a playbook from self-proposed tasks, updating it from each task’s feasibility and completion scores. These methods mainly favor tasks that are feasible or broaden environment coverage, whereas Daedalus calibrates tasks to expose failures the agent can learn to overcome.

paragraphs.en: We consider a base agent deployed in an agentic environment with no access to training tasks or an oracle verifier, and aim to improve its success rate without updating its weights. To this end, Daedalus spends a one-time budget of n n practice sessions, bootstrapping a bank of textual heuristics that the base agent receives in context at test time (Figure 2 ). Each session runs two nested loops: in the outer loop, an Explorer agent proposes a task and adjusts its difficulty; in the inner Solver loop (Figure 3 ), a Solver agent attempts the task while an Extractor agent derives a heuristic from its failures. Besides the Solver, generation involves several other LLM agents, including the Explorer and the Extractor, which we call auxiliary agents. We describe the Solver loop first, then task calibration and consolidation. Appendix A formalizes the approach in pseudo-code.
paragraphs.zh: 我们考虑一个部署在智能体环境中的基础智能体，该智能体无法访问训练任务或预言机验证器，我们的目标是在不更新其权重的情况下提高其成功率。 为此，Daedalus 会一次性投入 n 次实践会话的预算，构建一个文本启发式规则库，基础智能体在测试时会在上下文中接收到这些规则（图 2）。 每次会话都会运行两个嵌套循环：在外循环中，一个探索者智能体会提出任务并调整其难度；在内循环的求解器循环中（图 3），一个求解器智能体尝试完成任务，同时一个提取器智能体则从其失败中总结出启发式规则。 除了求解器之外，生成过程还涉及其他几个 LLM 智能体，包括探索者和提取器，我们将其称为辅助智能体。 我们将首先描述求解器循环，然后介绍任务校准与整合。 附录 A 以伪代码形式对该方法进行了形式化描述。

paragraphs.en: Each task consists of an instruction and explicit success conditions. The Solver attempts the task from a freshly reset environment, and an LLM Judge checks the resulting trajectory against the success conditions; we measure the Judge’s agreement with official benchmark verifiers in Section 5.1 . When an attempt fails, the Extractor writes a heuristic from the instruction and the failed trajectory, or revises the heuristic written after an earlier failure, and the Solver retries with it in context ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) . The Extractor does not see which success conditions were missed, which discourages task-specific fixes in favor of generalizable guidance. The loop stops once the Solver succeeds N s N_{s} consecutive times or fails N f N_{f} times in total, with three possible outcomes: the heuristic is accepted if the Solver failed at least once before these N s N_{s} successes; the task is too easy if the Solver never failed; and it is too hard if the Solver reached N f N_{f} failures. Whereas prior methods validate memories by the outcome of the trajectory they were drawn from ( Zhao et al., 2024 ; Fu et al., 2024 ; Allard et al., 2026 ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ) or by task feasibility ( Choi et al., 2026 ) , Daedalus thus tests the heuristic itself, and requiring N s N_{s} consecutive successes rather than a single one lowers the probability of accepting an ineffective heuristic after a success due to chance (Appendix C ).
paragraphs.zh: 每个任务都包含一个指令和明确的成功条件。 求解器从全新重置的环境中尝试完成任务，而大型语言模型评判器则根据成功条件检查由此产生的轨迹；我们在第 5.1 节中衡量了该评判器与官方基准验证器的一致性。 当一次尝试失败时，提取器会根据指令和失败的轨迹编写一个启发式规则，或修改之前失败后编写的启发式规则，然后求解器会结合该规则再次尝试（Shinn et al., 2023）。 提取器无法看到哪些成功条件未被满足，这有助于避免针对特定任务的修正，转而采用更具通用性的指导策略。 一旦求解器连续成功 N s N_{s} 次或总共失败 N f N_{f} 次，该循环就会停止，此时存在三种可能的结果：如果求解器在这些 N s N_{s} 次成功之前至少失败过一次，则接受该启发式规则；如果求解器从未失败，则说明任务过于简单；如果求解器达到了 N f N_{f} 次失败，则说明任务过于困难。 与此前通过轨迹结果（Zhao et al., 2024; Fu et al., 2024; Allard et al., 2026; Ouyang et al., 2026）或任务可行性（Choi et al., 2026）验证记忆的方法不同，Daedalus 直接测试启发式规则本身；此外，要求连续成功 N s N_{s} 次而非仅一次，降低了因偶然因素而在成功之后接受无效启发式规则的可能性（附录 C）。

paragraphs.en: In each session, the Explorer interacts with the environment, proposes a realistic task, and completes it itself to establish feasibility ( Shi et al., 2026 ; Ramrakhya et al., 2026 ) . Because only accepted tasks yield heuristics, the Solver loop outcome doubles as a difficulty signal: when a task is too easy or too hard, the Explorer receives this outcome along with its previous attempt and revises the task to be harder or easier, up to N r N_{r} times. A session that exhausts its refinements contributes no heuristic. As in proposer–solver curricula ( Yue et al., 2026 ) , this feedback steers generation toward the edge of the Solver’s capability, where failures are recoverable. In our main experiments, the Solver shares the base agent’s model, and we show in Section 4 that the resulting bank also transfers to base agents from other model families. Figure 4 shows how an example session unfolds.

sents.zh: 由于只有被接受的任务才能产生启发式方法，因此求解器循环的结果也同时充当难度信号：当任务过于简单或过于困难时，探索者会连同其之前的尝试一起收到这一结果，并调整任务使其更难或更简单，最多重复 N_r 次。

sents.en: A session that exhausts its refinements contributes no heuristic.
sents.zh: 用尽所有优化次数的会话不会产生任何启发式方法。

sents.en: As in proposer–solver curricula ( Yue et al., 2026 ) , this feedback steers generation toward the edge of the Solver’s capability, where failures are recoverable.
sents.zh: 与“提出者-求解器”课程设计（Yue 等人，2026）中的情况一样，这种反馈将生成过程引导至求解器能力边缘，即失败后仍能够恢复的临界点。

sents.en: In our main experiments, the Solver shares the base agent’s model, and we show in Section 4 that the resulting bank also transfers to base agents from other model families.
sents.zh: 在我们的主要实验中，求解器共享基础智能体的模型，我们在第 4 节中表明，由此生成的知识库也可以迁移到其他模型家族的基础智能体上。

paragraphs.en: Two components reduce generation cost (Section 5.1 ). Before the first session, a Surveyor explores the environment once and defines a target distribution of tasks across its areas, which the Explorer then follows to diversify the coverage of its tasks. In addition, after each session that required refinement, the refinement history is turned into guidelines that help the Explorer calibrate difficulty in later sessions.
paragraphs.zh: 两个组件降低了生成成本（第 5.1 节）。 在第一次会话之前，调查员会先对环境进行一次探索，并定义任务在各区域的目标分布，随后探索员将遵循该分布以多样化其任务的覆盖范围。 此外，在每次需要优化的会话结束后，优化历史都会被转化为指导方针，帮助探索员在后续会话中校准难度。

paragraphs.en: We run evaluations on three agentic benchmarks with different task types and environments: code-based app automation in AppWorld ( Trivedi et al., 2024 ) , conversational customer service in τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench ( Barres et al., 2026 ) , and business workflows with SaaS applications in AutomationBench ( Shepard and Salimans, 2026 ) . We evaluate agents on AppWorld’s normal test split, whose tasks use the same apps as the training split. On τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench, we use only the retail domain, since airline contains ground-truth errors ( Rabanser et al., 2026 ) , and the dual-control setting of telecom would require simulating user-side tools during exploration. Due to compute costs, we restrict AutomationBench to its Operations split, whose higher public scores ensure a non-trivial baseline.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在三种不同类型的任务和环境中，对三个智能体基准进行了评估：AppWorld 中的代码驱动型应用自动化（Trivedi 等人，2024）、τ²-bench 中的对话式客户服务（Barres 等人，2026），以及 AutomationBench 中涉及 SaaS 应用的业务工作流程（Shepard 和 Salimans，2026）。 我们在 AppWorld 的常规测试集上对智能体进行了评估，该测试集中的任务使用了与训练集相同的应用程序。 在 τ²-bench 中，我们仅使用零售领域，因为航空领域存在真实数据错误（Rabanser 等人，2026），而电信领域的双控制设置则需要模拟探索过程中的用户端工具。 由于计算成本问题，我们将 AutomationBench 限定在其 Operations 测试集上，该测试集较高的公开分数确保了其基准具有挑战性。

paragraphs.en: We compare Daedalus against a no-memory baseline, which measures the capability of the base agent alone, and six memory methods. To our knowledge, PREPING ( Choi et al., 2026 ) is the only existing method that also builds memory from self-generated tasks instead of training tasks. The other five build memory from the benchmark training tasks, and therefore have access to information that Daedalus does not. ExpeL ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) and AutoGuide ( Fu et al., 2024 ) contrast successful and failed retries of each training task to extract global insights and context-specific guidelines, respectively. ERL ( Allard et al., 2026 ) and ReasoningBank ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) instead reflect on a single attempt per task, with the environment reward and an LLM judge as the respective feedback signals. ACE ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) maintains an evolving playbook that it refines through incremental updates. Finally, to isolate the memory mechanism from task generation, we evaluate a Daedalus -curated variant that runs our Solver loop on the same training tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 Daedalus 与一个无记忆基线模型（用于衡量基础智能体本身的能力）以及六种记忆方法进行了比较。 据我们所知，PREPING（Choi 等人，2026）是唯一一种同样通过自我生成的任务而非训练任务来构建记忆的方法。 其余五种方法则是基于基准测试中的训练任务构建记忆，因此它们能够获取 Daedalus 无法获得的信息。 ExpeL（Zhao 等人，2024）和 AutoGuide（Fu 等人，2024）分别通过对比每个训练任务中成功与失败的重试过程，来提取全局性洞见和特定情境的指导方针。 ERL（Allard 等人，2026）和 ReasoningBank（Ouyang 等人，2026）则转而针对每个任务的单次尝试进行反思，分别以环境奖励和 LLM 判官作为反馈信号。 ACE（Zhang 等人，2026）会维护一个不断演进的策略手册，并通过增量更新对其进行优化。 最后，为了将记忆机制与任务生成过程分离开来，我们评估了一个由 Daedalus 精心挑选的变体版本，该版本在相同的训练任务上运行我们的 Solver 循环。

paragraphs.en: We split the public tasks of each benchmark into training tasks, from which we build reusable memory, and test tasks, on which we evaluate all methods. For AppWorld and τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench retail, we use the official splits (90/168 and 74/40 training/test tasks). For AutomationBench Operations, we split the 100 tasks 30/70, stratified by the number of services each task involves. Memory generation never accesses test instances and only uses environment states available to the baselines using training tasks (Appendix E ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们将每个基准测试的公开任务分为训练任务和测试任务：训练任务用于构建可重用的记忆，而测试任务则用于评估所有方法。 对于 AppWorld 和 τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench retail，我们使用官方划分的训练/测试任务（90/168 和 74/40）。 对于 AutomationBench Operations，我们将 100 个任务按 30/70 的比例划分，并依据每个任务涉及的服务数量进行分层。 记忆生成过程绝不会访问测试实例，仅使用基线模型通过训练任务可获得的环境状态（附录 E）。

paragraphs.en: To match the number of tasks available to the baselines, we run one Daedalus generation session per training task. The Explorer may refine each task up to N r = 5 N_{r}=5 times, and the Solver loop stops after N f = 8 N_{f}=8 failures. The loop accepts a heuristic after N s = 3 N_{s}=3 consecutive successes. We analyze these limits and the effect of accepted heuristics on their own tasks in Appendix C . We set these values from a few preliminary generation sessions on AppWorld and reuse them on τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench and AutomationBench without tuning. The solver harness is a basic agent loop that executes Python code in AppWorld and uses standard function calls elsewhere, with no capabilities beyond what each environment natively provides.
paragraphs.zh: 为了与基线模型可用的任务数量相匹配，我们为每个训练任务运行一次 Daedalus 生成会话。 探索器最多可以对每个任务进行 N r = 5 N_{r}=5 次优化，而求解器循环在发生 N f = 8 N_{f}=8 次失败后停止。 当连续成功 N s = 3 N_{s}=3 次时，该循环会接受一个启发式方法。 我们在附录 C 中分析了这些限制以及被接受的启发式方法对其自身任务的影响。 我们在 AppWorld 上通过几次初步的生成会话设置了这些值，并在 τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench 和 AutomationBench 上直接复用这些值，无需调整。 求解器框架是一个基础的智能体循环，它在 AppWorld 中执行 Python 代码，并在其他地方使用标准的函数调用，其能力不会超出各环境原生提供的功能。

paragraphs.en: All methods run a solver agent on tasks and delegate memory generation and retrieval to auxiliary agents, such as the Surveyor, Explorer, Judge, Extractor, and Consolidator in Daedalus . At test time, we evaluate a base agent that receives the resulting memory in context. We select two LLMs from the same family: the larger one for all auxiliary agents, and the smaller one for the solver and the base agent. By default, we use GPT-5.4 / GPT-5.4-mini on AppWorld and τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench, and GPT-5.6 Terra / GPT-5.6 Luna on AutomationBench, which is a more challenging benchmark. Appendix E lists the full configuration of each method.

paragraphs.en: For each method, we build one memory bank and average results over five independent inference runs, reporting the mean success rate (MSR) and pass^5 ( Yao et al., 2025 ) with their standard errors. We also report the inference cost for one evaluation run at OpenAI standard-tier API prices, assuming perfect prompt caching.

paragraphs.en: Daedalus raises the MSR of the base agent by 15.9, 10.0 and 4.3 points over the no-memory baseline on AppWorld, τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench and AutomationBench (Table 1 ). pass^5 increases by 1.7 × \times to 2.2 × \times , indicating that the method also improves consistency across runs. Daedalus also consistently outperforms PREPING on both metrics. On AppWorld and τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench, it does so at no extra inference cost over the no-memory baseline, mainly because the agent needs fewer turns (Figure 1 ).

paragraphs.en: We investigate to what extent Daedalus generalizes to various model families, and whether a bank generated with one model family also helps base agents from another. We therefore run Daedalus on AppWorld with auxiliary / solver model pairs from the Qwen and DeepSeek model families, and evaluate each memory bank with each base agent. Table 2 shows that all nine gains are positive, indicating that a base agent does not need the bank of its own model family. For example, GPT-5.4-mini gains as much from the Qwen bank as from its own (+16.8 against +15.9). DeepSeek-V4-Flash gains less (3.0 to 8.3 points), as its no-memory baseline of 80.6% leaves less room for improvement. Figure 1 extends this result to more base agent LLMs. With Daedalus memory, they all reach a higher MSR in fewer turns, showing that our method benefits a wide range of models.

paragraphs.en: This section examines each stage of Daedalus . For memory generation (Section 5.1 ), we ablate the pipeline components, validate the LLM judge against official benchmark verifiers, and vary the exploration budget and the auxiliary models. For inference (Section 5.2 ), we compare consolidating the bank and injecting it whole with retrieving heuristics at each turn. Finally, we test whether the generated tasks can serve as a proxy test set for ranking models (Section 5.3 ). Unless noted otherwise, all analyses use AppWorld, with GPT-5.4 for the auxiliary agents and GPT-5.4-mini for the Solver and base agent.

paragraphs.en: A mistaken judgment can misdirect task refinement or validate an unreliable heuristic. To assess our LLM judge, we compare it against benchmark-provided verifiers on official test sets. For each task, we let our Explorer inspect the environment and restate the benchmark’s oracle requirements as natural-language success conditions, as it would for a task it generated. The judge then receives the task instruction, these conditions, and the Solver trajectory, but not the official verifier or its verdict. For each benchmark with N N tasks, we judge one Solver trajectory per task five times and measure agreement with the official verifier ( κ bench \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}} ) and between repeated judgments ( κ inter \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}} ). Table 4 shows substantial agreement with the official verifiers ( κ bench > 0.7 \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}}>0.7 ) and consistent verdicts across calls ( κ inter > 0.8 \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}}>0.8 ). Precision exceeds recall on every benchmark, so the judge leans toward rejecting successes rather than accepting failures, which is the safer direction for accepting heuristics.
paragraphs.zh: 错误的判断可能会误导任务细化，或验证一个不可靠的经验法则。 为了评估我们的 LLM 判断器，我们在官方测试集上将其与基准提供的验证器进行比较。 对于每个任务，我们让探索者检查环境，并将基准的预言机要求重新表述为自然语言的成功条件，就像它处理自己生成的任务一样。 随后，判断器会收到任务说明、这些条件以及求解器的轨迹，但不会收到官方验证器或其裁决结果。 对于每个包含 N 个任务的基准，我们对每个任务的求解器轨迹进行五次判断，并测量其与官方验证器的一致性（κbench \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}}）以及重复判断之间的一致性（κinter \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}}）。 表 4 显示，该判断器与官方验证器具有高度一致性（κbench > 0.7 \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}}>0.7），且在不同调用中的裁决结果保持一致（κinter > 0.8 \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}}>0.8）。 在所有基准中，精确度均高于召回率，因此该判断器更倾向于拒绝成功结果而非接受失败结果，这是接受经验法则时更安全的选择。

sents.en: A mistaken judgment can misdirect task refinement or validate an unreliable heuristic.

sents.zh: 为了评估我们的 LLM 判断器，我们在官方测试集上将其与基准提供的验证器进行比较。

sents.en: For each task, we let our Explorer inspect the environment and restate the benchmark’s oracle requirements as natural-language success conditions, as it would for a task it generated.
sents.zh: 对于每个任务，我们让探索者检查环境，并将基准的预言机要求重新表述为自然语言的成功条件，就像它处理自己生成的任务一样。

sents.en: For each benchmark with N N tasks, we judge one Solver trajectory per task five times and measure agreement with the official verifier ( κ bench \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}} ) and between repeated judgments ( κ inter \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}} ).
sents.zh: 对于每个包含 N 个任务的基准，我们对每个任务的求解器轨迹进行五次判断，并测量其与官方验证器的一致性（κbench \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}}）以及重复判断之间的一致性（κinter \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}}）。

sents.en: Table 4 shows substantial agreement with the official verifiers ( κ bench > 0.7 \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}}>0.7 ) and consistent verdicts across calls ( κ inter > 0.8 \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}}>0.8 ).
sents.zh: 表 4 显示，该判断器与官方验证器具有高度一致性（κbench > 0.7 \kappa_{\mathrm{bench}}>0.7），且在不同调用中的裁决结果保持一致（κinter > 0.8 \kappa_{\mathrm{inter}}>0.8）。

sents.en: Precision exceeds recall on every benchmark, so the judge leans toward rejecting successes rather than accepting failures, which is the safer direction for accepting heuristics.

paragraphs.en: We study how performance depends on the exploration budget by continuing a generation run up to 140 sessions and evaluating the memory at successive checkpoints (Figure 6 ). Five sessions already deliver more than half of the improvement reached at the 90-session peak. Beyond 90 sessions, MSR decreases even as the bank grows. A hierarchical consolidation, designed to scale to large banks, does not recover the loss (54.6 vs. 53.7 MSR): with a larger bank, consolidation misstates the scope of some heuristics, and such minor changes can have a large impact on specific parts of the test distribution (Appendix B ). The early gains matter more in practice, since they make a useful memory affordable after only a few sessions.

paragraphs.en: Heuristics accepted in separate sessions often overlap, which raises two design questions at inference: whether to consolidate them into a compact bank, and whether to inject that whole bank or retrieve some heuristics at each turn. Injected at task start, the consolidated bank is both the best-performing and the cheapest option, improving MSR by 10.7 points over the unconsolidated heuristics while considerably shortening the context; deduplication alone yields no significant gain (Table 6 ). We then test whether retrieval can select more relevant heuristics per turn, comparing BM25, Qwen3-Embedding-4B ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) , and a random control, each retrieving five heuristics per turn (Appendix D ). All three improve over the no-memory baseline by up to 10 MSR points but do not differ significantly. A plausible reason is that useful heuristics are not necessarily semantically similar to the current step: retrieving them is an oblique retrieval problem, in which relevance is latent rather than expressed in the text ( Tchuindjo et al., 2026 ) . In line with this, retrieving more heuristics with BM25 improves success, but stays below whole-bank injection (58.2% at k = 30 k{=}30 ; Figure 7 ). At this scale, injecting the whole bank once at task start is thus the most effective option we tested, while larger banks would call for retrievers suited to oblique queries.

paragraphs.en: Environments without training tasks usually lack a test set as well, which makes it hard to compare agents on them. We test whether the tasks generated by Daedalus can fill this role by evaluating nine models without memory on the 81 accepted tasks of the 90-session AppWorld run and on the AppWorld normal test split, with three runs per task set. Rankings are strongly aligned for both MSR and pass^3 (Kendall’s τ = 0.89 \tau=0.89 , p < .001 p<.001 for both), with 34 of 36 model pairs ordered consistently in each case (Figure 8 ). Absolute success rates differ, as the generated tasks were calibrated to GPT-5.4-mini, but the relative order of models is preserved. These results suggest that Daedalus -generated tasks can serve as a proxy for ranking models when no curated test set is available.
paragraphs.zh: 没有训练任务的环境通常也缺乏测试集，这使得在这些环境中比较不同智能体变得困难。 我们通过评估九个无记忆模型在 AppWorld 90 次运行中接受的 81 个任务以及 AppWorld 常规测试集上的表现，每个任务集进行三次运行，以检验 Daedalus 生成的任务是否能填补这一空白。 无论是 MSR 还是 pass^3，排名结果都高度一致（Kendall’s τ = 0.89 \tau=0.89，两者均 p < .001 p<.001），在每种情况下，36 对模型中有 34 对的顺序保持一致（图 8）。 绝对成功率存在差异，因为生成的任务是根据 GPT-5.4-mini 校准的，但模型之间的相对顺序保持不变。 这些结果表明，在没有可用精选测试集的情况下，Daedalus 生成的任务可以作为模型排名的替代指标。

paragraphs.en: Memory-based agents usually learn from curated tasks and an existing verifier, which a new environment does not provide. Daedalus removes the need for both: the agent builds its memory by practicing on calibrated tasks it generates itself, and keeps a heuristic only once it has turned one of the solver’s failures into repeated success. Across three benchmarks, the resulting memory is the strongest among methods without training tasks and competitive with methods that require them, at marginal or no additional inference cost. The main reason behind this improvement is validation: heuristics drawn from exploration alone hurt the agent, whereas those grounded in its failures and confirmed empirically improve it. Additionally, Daedalus generates memory that transfers across model families, and tasks that rank models consistently with curated benchmarks, suggesting that it can also supply evaluation data where none exists.
paragraphs.zh: 基于记忆的智能体通常从精心挑选的任务和现有的验证器中学习，而新环境并不具备这些条件。 Daedalus 消除了这两者的必要性：智能体通过练习自己生成的校准任务来构建记忆，并且只有在将求解器的某次失败转化为持续成功之后，才会保留启发式方法。 在三项基准测试中，由此产生的记忆在没有训练任务的算法中表现最强，与需要训练任务的算法相比也具备竞争力，同时几乎没有或完全没有额外的推理成本。 这种改进的主要原因在于验证：仅从探索中获得的启发式方法会损害智能体，而基于其失败经验并通过实证确认的启发式方法则能提升其性能。 此外，Daedalus 生成的记忆可以在不同模型家族之间迁移，其生成的任务也能与精心挑选的基准测试保持一致的模型排名，这表明它还可以在没有现有评估数据的情况下提供评估数据。

paragraphs.en: On AppWorld, performance declined beyond 90 sessions as the memory grew, which raises open questions for scaling: how the composition and coverage of the bank vary across environments, how heuristics should be consolidated as the bank grows, and which retrieval mechanisms can best exploit large memories at inference time. paragraphs.en: To test whether the 140-session bank is too large for a single consolidation call, we also consolidate its 130 heuristics hierarchically: we split them at random into eight groups and merge these pairwise with the same prompt (Prompt G.1 ) until one bank remains ( 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 8\to 4\to 2\to 1 ). Both 140-session banks fall below the 90-session bank overall, yet on the 131 Other tasks they nearly match it (Table 7 , shaded): most of the gap sits in three small categories, where a few heuristics lost their scope. The single call narrows the 90-session rule to “enumerate every matching container” , so the Solver reads a single page of playlists or friends; the hierarchical merge broadens a note on public playlists into locating any playlist with is_public=True , which hides private ones.
paragraphs.zh: 为了测试包含 140 个会话的银行是否过大，无法通过单次合并调用处理，我们还对其中的 130 条启发式规则进行了分层合并：我们随机将其分为八组，并使用相同的提示（提示 G.1）两两合并，直到只剩下一个银行（8 → 4 → 2 → 1）。 两个包含 140 个会话的银行在整体表现上均低于包含 90 个会话的银行，但在 131 个“其他任务”上，它们几乎与之相当（表 7，阴影部分）：大部分差距集中在三个小类别中，这些类别中的少数启发式规则失去了其适用范围。 单次调用将 90 个会话的规则简化为“枚举所有匹配的容器”，因此求解器只需读取播放列表或好友的单个页面；而分层合并则会将关于公开播放列表的说明扩展为定位任何 is_public=True 的播放列表，从而隐藏了私有播放列表。

The generation loop of Daedalus is controlled by a failure limit N f N_{f} , which caps the number of failed solver attempts at a task, and a number of refinements N r N_{r} which sets the number of times the explorer may revise a task that is too easy or too hard. Low limits lose heuristics on the hardest tasks, which are the ones where memory helps most. High limits spend compute on tasks the Solver cannot solve or the Explorer cannot calibrate. We set N f = 8 N_{f}=8 and N r = 5 N_{r}=5 after a few preliminary sessions and validate them on the 90-session AppWorld run (Figure 9 ). Most heuristics are accepted after one or two failures, but a tail of sessions need up to seven, so a smaller N f N_{f} would lose heuristics on the hardest feasible tasks. Additionally, most sessions need at most two refinements and only a handful need four or five, which justifies our choice of N r = 5 N_{r}=5 .
paragraphs.zh: Daedalus 的生成循环由一个失败阈值 N f N_{f}（用于限制任务中求解器尝试失败的最大次数）和一次精炼次数 N r N_{r}（用于规定探索者可以修订过于简单或过于困难的任务的次数）进行控制。 较低的阈值会导致在最困难的任务上失去启发式方法，而这些任务正是记忆能发挥最大帮助作用的场景。 较高的阈值会将计算资源消耗在求解器无法解决或探索者无法校准的任务上。 经过几次初步运行后，我们将 N f = 8 N_{f}=8 和 N r = 5 N_{r}=5，并在包含 90 次运行的 AppWorld 实验中验证了这些参数（图 9）。 大多数启发式方法在一次或两次失败后就会被接受，但少数运行需要多达七次尝试，因此较小的 N f N_{f} 会导致在最困难的可行任务上失去启发式方法。 此外，大多数运行最多只需要两次精炼，只有极少数运行需要四次或五次，这为我们选择 N r = 5 N_{r}=5 提供了依据。

paragraphs.en: On the official AppWorld tasks, the benchmark provides the tasks and their verdicts, so the extractor is the only auxiliary agent that affects the memory. We vary its model and reasoning effort, while keeping GPT-5.4-mini as the solver (Table 8 ). With GPT-5.4-mini at high reasoning effort instead of GPT-5.4, the gain over the no-memory baseline falls from 16.5 to 12.8 MSR points. Disabling reasoning lowers it further to 9.5 points, while pass^5 does not change. Every extractor still improves the solver by a clear margin, so extraction from curated trajectories is robust to the choice of model. The drop from GPT-5.4 to GPT-5.4-mini (3.7 MSR points) is also smaller than on self-generated tasks (9.0 points, Section 5.1 ), which suggests that the other auxiliary roles account for most of the drop in that setting.
paragraphs.zh: 在官方的 AppWorld 任务中，基准测试提供了任务及其判定结果，因此提取器是唯一影响记忆的智能体辅助工具。 我们调整其模型和推理强度，同时保持使用 GPT-5.4-mini 作为求解器（表 8）。 当使用高推理强度的 GPT-5.4-mini 而非 GPT-5.4 时，相比无记忆基线的提升从 16.5 降至 12.8 MSR 分。 禁用推理后，该数值进一步降至 9.5 分，而 pass^5 的结果则未发生变化。 每种提取器都能以明显优势提升求解器的表现，因此从精选轨迹中提取信息对模型的选择具有鲁棒性。 从 GPT-5.4 到 GPT-5.4-mini 的性能下降（3.7 MSR 分）也小于自生成任务中的下降幅度（9.0 分，第 5.1 节），这表明在该设置中，其他辅助角色导致了大部分性能下降。

paragraphs.en: Since the solver is an LLM agent, it is inherently stochastic and an ineffective heuristic could pass the acceptance rule by chance. To quantify to what extent the heuristics we accept raise the solver’s success rate, we run the solver three times on each of the 81 accepted AppWorld tasks, with and without their accepted heuristic, and grade it with the LLM Judge. With its heuristic in context, the solver’s MSR rises from 66.7% to 77.0% and its pass^3 from 40.7% to 55.6%. We assess these gains with a paired bootstrap, which resamples the 81 tasks with replacement 10,000 times while keeping each task’s two conditions together, so that differences in difficulty between tasks do not inflate the variance. The resulting 95% confidence intervals are [2.1, 18.5] points for MSR and [1.2, 28.4] points for pass^3, and both exclude zero.
paragraphs.zh: 由于求解器是一个 LLM 智能体，其本身具有随机性，因此低效的启发式方法可能偶然通过接受规则。 为了量化我们所接受的启发式方法在多大程度上提升了求解器的成功率，我们对 81 个被接受的 AppWorld 任务中的每个任务运行三次求解器：一次使用已接受的启发式方法，一次不使用，并由 LLM 裁判进行评分。 当将启发式方法纳入上下文时，求解器的 MSR 从 66.7% 提升至 77.0%，其 pass^3 则从 40.7% 提升至 55.6%。 我们采用配对自助法来评估这些提升：该方法在保留每个任务的两个条件组合不变的前提下，对 81 个任务进行有放回重采样 10,000 次，从而避免任务间难度差异导致方差膨胀。 由此得到的 95% 置信区间为：MSR 的 [2.1, 18.5] 个百分点，pass^3 的 [1.2, 28.4] 个百分点，且两者均不包含零。

paragraphs.en: We investigate three axes that control how the heuristic bank is used at inference: the retrieval method and the number of retrieved heuristics, the source of the retrieval query, and the injection policy (Figure 10 ). All experiments use the 65-heuristic consolidated bank generated on AppWorld with GPT-5.4, evaluated on the 168 tasks of test_normal over five runs with GPT-5.4-mini as the solver. Unless stated otherwise, retrieval uses the agent’s reasoning from the previous turn as query ( Pre-Gen ), retrieves k = 5 k{=}5 heuristics per turn, and keeps them in context with deduplication ( Cumulative, deduplicated ); this is the configuration reported in Table 6 .
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了三个控制推理阶段启发式银行使用方式的关键因素：检索方法以及所检索启发式的数量、检索查询的来源，以及注入策略（图 10）。 所有实验均使用在 AppWorld 上通过 GPT-5.4 生成的包含 65 个启发式的整合银行，并在 test_normal 的 168 项任务上进行评估，评估过程重复五次，使用 GPT-5.4-mini 作为求解器。 除非另有说明，否则检索将以智能体上一轮推理结果作为查询（Pre-Gen），每轮检索 k = 5 个启发式，并通过去重将其保留在上下文中（Cumulative, deduplicated）；这是表 6 中报告的配置。

paragraphs.en: At k = 5 k{=}5 , dense retrieval with Qwen3-Embedding-4B, sparse retrieval with BM25, and random selection do not differ significantly (Table 6 ), indicating that on a consolidated bank, any five heuristics carry similar information regardless of how they are chosen. Retrieval only approaches whole-bank injection once it surfaces about half of the bank per turn; for a bank of 3.1k tokens, retrieving a subset therefore brings no practical benefit.

paragraphs.en: In Table 10 , the retriever is fixed and only the way retrieved heuristics enter the context changes. Transient shows them for the current call and then drops them from the history. The other three policies keep them in the history and differ only in how they treat a heuristic that is retrieved again. With repetition appends it anyway, Deduplicated skips it, and No replacement removes it from the candidates altogether, so that each turn brings five heuristics the agent has not seen before. Retention is the dominant factor: Transient is the weakest policy (48.5 MSR), and its pass^5 of 13.1 falls below the no-memory baseline. Repeating heuristics already in context also hurts relative to deduplication (50.0 vs. 54.3 MSR), suggesting that redundant context harms multi-turn decision-making. No replacement exposes the solver to the most distinct heuristics (46.0 on average) and achieves the best retrieved-subset MSR (56.0), yet remains below whole-bank injection at task start (60.2). The same pattern holds for the whole bank: injecting it transiently at every turn ( All @ Turn ) underperforms injecting it once in the system prompt ( All @ Start ) on both metrics and at higher cost, consistent with the benefit of persistent guidance.
paragraphs.zh: 在表 10 中，检索器是固定的，只有被检索到的启发式方法进入上下文的方式会发生变化。 Transient 模式会在当前调用时显示这些启发式方法，然后将其从历史记录中移除。 另外三种策略会将它们保留在历史记录中，唯一的区别在于如何处理再次被检索到的启发式方法。 重复策略无论如何都会追加它，去重策略会跳过它，而无替换策略则完全将其从候选项中移除，因此每个回合都会带来智能体此前未见过的五个启发式方法。 保留策略是主导因素：Transient 是最弱的策略（48.5 MSR），其 pass^5 为 13.1，甚至低于无记忆基线。 重复使用上下文中已有的启发式方法相较于去重策略表现也更差（50.0 vs. 54.3 MSR），这表明冗余的上下文会损害多回合决策能力。 无替换策略让求解器接触到最多样化的启发式方法（平均 46.0），并实现了最佳检索子集 MSR（56.0），但仍低于任务开始时注入整个知识库的表现（60.2）。 在整个知识库上也能观察到相同模式：在每个回合临时注入（All @ Turn）在两项指标上的表现均不如一次性在系统提示中注入（All @ Start），且成本更高，这与持久性指导的优势一致。

paragraphs.en: Every method uses the same pair of LLMs on a given benchmark (Table 11 ). The solver and the base agent run on the smaller model, and every auxiliary agent runs on the larger model. This includes roles that some original implementations assign to the solver model: the ExpeL reflector, the AutoGuide context module, the ReasoningBank extractor and judge, and the PREPING proposer, validator and curator. We raise them to the larger model so that no method is limited by a weaker auxiliary model. On τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench, the user simulator is gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 for all methods, as per the original benchmark implementation.

paragraphs.en: In the retail domain, the tool modify_pending_order_items assigns the price and options of the last exchanged pair to every item of a multi-item call, so two equally correct solutions that list the same items in a different order reach different database states and receive different grades. paragraphs.en: We reimplement ExpeL, ERL, AutoGuide, ReasoningBank and ACE on top of our solver harness, with the hyperparameters of Table 13 . For ExpeL, the insight list cap follows the authors’ released code, and we use L = 3 L=3 instead of the paper’s 4 to 8 because our trajectories are much longer. For AutoGuide, we use k = 3 k=3 , the best value in the paper’s own ablation. In ERL, we use both successful and failed attempts to create heuristics. ReasoningBank builds its bank on the training tasks, processed in parallel waves, and the bank is frozen at test time so we do not use test-time scaling (MaTTS). We use text-embedding-3-large as the embedding model to retrieve memories. For ACE, we use its offline variant without ground truth: each training task is solved once, sequentially, and a reflector and a curator turn every trajectory into ADD operations on the playbook, with no success signal. We start from an empty playbook, run the reflector and the curator on gpt-5.4 , and inject the whole playbook at the start of each test task. For PREPING, we run the authors’ released code and inject the whole playbook at the start of each test task. On τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench, its task proposer also sees sampled database records, without which it could not write feasible tasks.

paragraphs.en: Daedalus spends more solver rollouts than any baseline, about 6 times more than ExpeL and 14 times more than single-attempt methods (Table 14 ). Most of this gap is the cost of not having training tasks. Of the 1,225 rollouts, 520 are spent on the explorer’s first version of each task, which is close to the 592 rollouts of Daedalus -curated on the training tasks, and the remaining 705 are spent on refined versions of tasks that were too easy or too hard. The Solver loop itself therefore costs about as much on generated tasks as on curated ones, and task calibration roughly doubles it. These rollouts use the small Solver model, so they account for a minor share of the generation cost reported in Table 3 , which is dominated by the explorer and the judge.

paragraphs.en: The original AppWorld solver prompt ( Trivedi et al., 2024 ) contains extensive human-written heuristics for the environment, so we replace it with a simplified version (Prompt G.2 , inserted into the shared solver template of Prompt G.1 ) to evaluate all methods with less hand-engineered guidance.
